messages:
jordan (partnerships): Heads up — Datadog asked if we can ship a first-class OpenTelemetry + Datadog dashboard bundle for Redwood Dedicated and Private. They want a joint beta/demo in ~3 weeks. Who can own tech scoping? :eyes:
sophia (eng-observability): I can take tech scope. Need to decide which signals we surface: traces, span attributes, tokenized generation metrics, prefix cache hit rates, per-model p99 latencies.
raj (platform): We should expose model routing and cache metrics as OTLP metrics + spans. Also need a small manifest that maps our metric names to Datadog metrics for the dashboard.
emily (marketing): Great — if we hit the timeline marketing can coordinate a joint announcement + webinar. Need logo assets and a 1-paragraph partner quote from Datadog legal.
jordan (partnerships): I'll loop in the Datadog partner PM. Action items: 1) tech spec (sophia) 2) dashboard JSON + mapping (raj) 3) security/compliance checklist (sam) 4) marketing assets (emily).
sophia (eng-observability): Quick question: for Private customers we can't leak raw prompts. We should only send aggregated prompt metadata and token counts to Datadog. Agreed?
sam (security): Agreed. Also require opt-in toggle in the config and documented KMS workflow for Datadog API key in Private deployments. Will stub a checklist.
raj (platform): On implementation: recommend shipping an OTEL collector config snippet + a sample Datadog Dashboard JSON. Example OTEL collector block for Dedicated:

```
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
      http:
exporters:
  datadog:
    api:
      key: "${DD_API_KEY}" # use env / KMS wrapper for private
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [datadog]
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [datadog]
```

raj (platform): We'll include a note about sampling: default 1% for user traffic, 100% for internal SRE traces.
sophia (eng-observability): For spans, include these attributes: model.name, model.version, route.id, shard.id, cache.hit (bool), prompt.token_count, response.token_count. Mapping doc will show datadog tags.
emily (marketing): For the webinar: propose short demo + customer use case (observability of cost regressions when a new model rollout increases token count). Need a simple slide + gif.
jordan (partnerships): Legal/contract question: do we need a simple MOU? emily said Datadog wants co-branded materials.
legal-bot: Heads up — any co-branded customer-facing assets require partner marketing addendum. Recommend starting with a non-binding PR plan and route to legal for the addendum.
sam (security): Also flag: for Private/on-prem, no outbound traffic by default. Provide an agent-based forwarding option and an explicit admin opt-in. Document firewall rules.
sophia (eng-observability): Timeline proposal: day 0-4 tech spec, day 5-10 implement collector + dashboard, day 11-14 internal QA + security review, day 15-18 partner demo + iterate, day 19-21 marketing prep and announce. Can we compress?
emily (marketing): That works but push legal signoff parallel — if we wait for final legal we miss webinar window.
jordan (partnerships): I'll run the partner PM schedule and try to secure a demo slot on day 16. Datadog asked for a short checklist of APIs we'll call and a sample dashboard JSON.
raj (platform): I'll drop a sample dashboard JSON in the shared drive and a mapping file to Datadog metric names. Will also add a flag in the Dedicated UI to toggle "share telemetry with Datadog" behind admin controls.
sophia (eng-observability): One more item — instrument our internal reranker and generation cache so the dashboard can show cache hit rate vs p99 latency. Small schema below:

- metric: redwood.cache.hit_rate (gauge)
- metric: redwood.model.p99_latency_ms (histogram)
- span attr: redwood.cache.hit (bool)

sophia (eng-observability): I'll post the full tech spec by EOD tomorrow.
emily (marketing): Ping me when you post the spec so we can draft the partner blog outline. :+1:
jordan (partnerships): Thanks everyone. I'll start the Datadog PM thread and post notes here. :rocket:
